about: Background transcription queue vectors (PLAN.md section 4.9 'Queue rules', Windows 18.10), shared by the macOS and Windows apps. timing: 'immediate' | 'whenIdle' (the finalPassTiming setting). state: 'waiting' | 'running' | 'suspended' | 'done' | 'failed'. jobs are listed in queue order (first in first); ids are plain strings. sessionActive: a session is Starting, Recording, Paused, or Stopping. foregroundWaiting: number of foreground engine calls waiting (live chunks, language detection, File mode, History re-runs). A queued job may run when foregroundWaiting <= 0 and, for whenIdle, sessionActive is false. next: if a job is running, 'suspend' the first running job (queue order) when running is not allowed, else 'none'; with nothing running and running allowed, 'resume' the first suspended job, else 'start' the first waiting job, else 'none'; done and failed jobs are skipped. expect.action is start | resume | suspend | none and expect.job the job id (null for none). Invalid inputs (notes starting with 'invalid') are tolerated, never asserted: two running jobs consider only the first; a running job behind a waiting or suspended one is not preempted; a suspended job is resumed before an earlier waiting one; a negative foregroundWaiting counts as 0. shouldYield is true exactly when next would suspend a running job. presentsNotes: a finished job opens its notes flow only when no session is active and no notes flow is on screen. quitNeedsConfirmation is the count of waiting, running, and suspended jobs; blocksUpdateInstall is true when that count is above 0. Mirrors TranscriptionQueuePolicyTests.swift. The 'manual' section at the end (PLAN.md 4.11, 18.12) adds a third timing and is read by the Windows app only until the Mac port; the sections above never use it and are unchanged.

manual.about: Manual final pass vectors (PLAN.md 4.11 'Manual final passes', Windows 18.12): timing 'manual' ("When I start them") adds a per-job in-memory released flag; jobs carry released: true|false (an absent flag means false). A pending job (waiting, running, suspended) is held when the timing is manual and it is not released; the flag is ignored under immediate and whenIdle, which the cases with those timings show. Running is allowed under manual exactly as under whenIdle: foregroundWaiting <= 0 (a negative count is 0) and sessionActive false. next under manual: if a job is running, 'suspend' the first running job (queue order) when it is not released or when running is not allowed, else 'none'; with nothing running and running allowed, 'resume' the first released suspended job, else 'start' the first released waiting job, else 'none'. Held jobs are never started or resumed, so a released job may run past an earlier held one; among released jobs queue order decides (releasing job 2 before job 1 does not let job 2 jump), and a released suspended job is resumed before an earlier released waiting one. done and failed jobs are skipped. Notes starting with 'invalid' are tolerated inputs. shouldYield takes the running job's released flag: true when the timing is manual and it is not released, or when running is not allowed; it is true exactly when next would suspend a running job. blocksUpdateInstall under manual is true when a pending job is released or running (held waiting and held suspended jobs are in queue.json and come back held after the relaunch); under the other timings it is true when any job is pending. allPendingHeld is true under manual when at least one job is pending and every pending job is not released (a running job that is not released counts as held); it picks the quit alert's second line. quitNeedsConfirmation still counts every pending job (the section above).
